articles.summary: The Thomas Guide Is a map that painstakingly details how to navigate Los Angeles by car. It’s a spiral-bound relic that almost none of your junior executives remember. Your assistant thinks it’s a ranking of pale British heartthrobs.
body: I’ll tell my assistants — not my current two, because they’ve gotten it — but I ask them to call [someone] and I’ll follow up and ask if they talked to them. The assistants will say, “Well, I texted.” But that’s not what I asked for. I asked you to call. I understand that texts and DMs are how we have the conversation now, but I like the personal [nature] of a phone call. I’ll also have my assistant call back after 15-20 minutes. You’re going to start seeing a lot of new development around that. Steve Jobs [once spoke about] a study about humans. That they were the slowest-moving mammals until the invention of the bicycle, then became the fastest. So, whatever [Hollywood looks like in the future], we’ll still need legs to pedal those bikes.

articles.title: ‘Digger’ First Reactions Split Over Tom Cruise’s ‘Baffling,’ ‘Unpleasant’ and ‘Brave’ New Movie: ‘The Divide on This Is Going to Be Wide’
articles.summary: Tom Cruise’s star vehicle “Digger” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who have been left divided by the satirical black comedy. The latest directorial effort from “Birdman” and “The Revenant” Oscar winner Alejandro González Iñárritu is being called everything from “baffling” to…
body: Anne Thompson of IndieWire was also high on the movie, calling it “a brave and gorgeous art film that will not score with mainstream audiences but will play best for the Academy, especially crafts and actors.”

“Digger” stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy tycoon who must save the world when one of his oil rigs malfunctions and causes an environmental catastrophe across the planet. The film’s supporting cast includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons.

For Cruise, “Digger” notably marks his return to adult-oriented drama after more than a decade playing action movie heroes. In the last 10 years, Cruise’s only non-action movie is the 2017 crime comedy “American Made.” One would have to go back 20 years to add more non-action movies to Cruise’s roster, such as the musical “Rock of Ages,” the political drama “Lions for Lambs,” the comedy “Tropic Thunder” and the historical thriller “Valkyrie.” Cruise’s return to more dramatic fare has raised the eyebrows of Oscar pundits since “Digger” was announced a few years ago, but the wildly divisive reactions to “Digger” may upend his expected awards campaign.

articles.title: Post your questions for Miranda Richardson
articles.summary: She has lit up screens large and small playing Ruth Ellis, Rita Skeeter, Barbara Castle and the hilarious Queenie in Blackadder. Alternatively, you could ask about birds of prey, orangutans or playing the cello.
body: Judging by the size of her awards cupboard, Miranda Richardson has had quite the career. She won a Bafta for the 1992 psychological drama Damage, opposite Jeremy Irons, and Golden Globes for the 1991 historical drama Enchanted April and the 1994 Nazi thriller Fatherland, and was Oscar-nominated for both Damage and the 1994 historical drama Tom & Viv. Her other notable performances include IRA member Jude in The Crying Game, Ruth Ellis in Dance With a Stranger and Lady Van Tassel in Sleepy Hollow.

She’s pretty handy at comedy, too – and probably just as familiar for playing acid-tongued Daily Prophet journalist Rita Skeeter in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the murderous chicken-farm owner Mrs Tweedy in Chicken Run and, of course, the gloriously unhinged Queenie in Blackadder II: “I may have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a concrete elephant.”

articles.title: Dolly Parton free book scheme to expand in London
articles.summary: The late singer's Imagination Library posts children a free book every month until they turn five.
body: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which posts children a free book every month until their fifth birthday, is to double the number of London boroughs it covers.
The scheme, which runs in five boroughs, will expand to 10 boroughs.
It comes a month after the country singer died at the age of 80. She set up the library in 1995 in tribute to her father, who could not read or write.
Funded by the Postcode Lottery, the expansion of the scheme will make 157,000 children eligible.

articles.title: Earl Spencer should pull Diana book from shelves, Piers Morgan says
articles.summary: Princess Diana's brother apologised to Morgan for a factual error in his memoir. Morgan said he is "pursuing legal action" against Spencer.
body: Piers Morgan has called for Earl Spencer's book about Princess Diana to be pulled from the shelves over a factual error.

Earl Spencer, Princess Diana's brother, apologised to Morgan for incorrectly describing him in the memoir as the editor of the Daily Mirror when the Mirror Group published "highly intrusive photographs of Princess Diana at the gym" in 1993.

Speaking to the BBC, Morgan said he accepted the apology but that his lawyers would be "laying out that we want the offending pages to be removed from this book. And if that means they pulp the first edition, so be it".
The BBC understands Penguin, the publishers of Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, will be amending this one point in future editions of the book.
points: Morgan said he is "pursuing legal action" against Spencer.

articles.title: Brigitte Bardot’s personal items sell for nearly €1m at auction in Paris
articles.summary: Dog collars, guitars and self-portraits among 285 objects, with money going to her animal welfare foundation and son. An auction of the French film star turned animal rights activist Brigitte Bardot’s personal items has fetched nearly €1m (£858,000, US$1.15m, A$1.61m) in Paris, almost 20 times the…
body: A total of 285 objects were auctioned, ranging from straw hats, sunglasses and nightgowns to tableware and furniture from Bardot’s homes in Paris and Saint-Tropez, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported.

Bardot, who died in December aged 91, retired from acting in the 1970s and became an outspoken campaigner for animal rights. She also became increasingly active politically on the far right, alienating some fans in her later life with her hardline views on immigration. Bardot was convicted five times for hate speech, particularly about Muslims, and up until her death she expressed her pleasure at the rising share of the vote gained by the anti-immigration National Rally party.
The proceeds from the auction will go to her animal welfare foundation and to Nicolas-Jacques Charrier, her only child.

Founded by the actor in 1986, the Brigitte Bardot Foundation says it has taken in 13,000 animals through four shelters and 150 partner facilities, supports 350 groups in France and operates in 70 countries.

articles.title: Booker Prize judges reveal shortlisted novels after selection 'tussle'
articles.summary: Past Booker winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the nominees for this year's award.
body: Past Booker Prize winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart have been shortlisted for the prestigious literary award again, after a selection process that the judges described as "a tussle".
Jamaican writer James is nominated this year for his latest novel The Disappearers; while Scottish author Stuart is shortlisted for John of John.
This year's other contenders are award-winning US novelist Elizabeth Strout, and British authors M John Harrison, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry.
But seven books that appeared on the longlist in July have been jettisoned, and Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the judging panel, said agreeing on the final six "has been, to put it mildly, hard work".
points: Past Booker winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the nominees for this year's award.

articles.title: Sir Sean Connery's family plans new filmmaking centre in Edinburgh
articles.summary: It will be named after the James Bond actor, who worked as a milkman in the Scottish capital before becoming a Hollywood star.
body: The family of Sir Sean Connery has announced plans for a new filmmaking centre in Edinburgh.
His children say they want it to provide training for the next generation of Scotland's film and TV talent and help them build lasting careers.

They said their father "understood that while talent may be distributed equally, opportunity is not, and that those who demonstrate determination and endeavour should have the chance to fulfill their potential".
They have unveiled plans to open the NFTS Sean Connery Institute in Edinburgh city centre within the next 18 months.
